what.text: Gonadorelin is a synthetic copy of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH, also called LHRH), a 10-amino-acid peptide made by the hypothalamus. It has the same amino acid sequence as the body’s own hormone.

items.text: GnRH makes the pituitary release LH and FSH, the hormones that drive testosterone and sperm production in the testes.

src.label: Factrel (gonadorelin) veterinary label, Zoetis, DailyMed

items.text: In the body GnRH is released in pulses. In men whose own GnRH is missing (congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism), studies gave gonadorelin in pulses from a small pump under the skin to restart this signal.

src.label: Zhang et al., Am J Mens Health

what.text: Gonadorelin was FDA approved (Factrel, Lutrepulse), but every human product is now discontinued. Its use alongside testosterone therapy has no published human studies.

research.text: The published studies in men test pulsatile gonadorelin pumps in congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, mostly small and not randomized. No published human study of gonadorelin given alongside testosterone therapy (TRT) was found. Two 2026 reviews say evidence for peptides used to protect fertility on TRT is limited.

research.title: Gonadorelin pump vs hCG/hMG in congenital hypogonadism (Zhang et al.)

facts.v: 28 men with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and no sperm: 10 on a gonadorelin pump, 18 on hCG plus hMG injections
time until sperm appeared; testis volume, penile length, hormones, side effects

research.found: Sperm appeared earlier with the pump (median 6 vs 14 months). Sperm appeared in 90% vs 83.3%, a difference that was not significant. Skin redness and hardening at the pump site was a common side effect.

src.label: Zhang et al., Am J Mens Health

research.title: Pulsatile gonadorelin and bone in young men with hypogonadism (Li et al.)

facts.v: observational; patients compared with healthy controls at baseline, then measured again after treatment
22 young men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, 20 healthy controls

research.found: At baseline, osteoporosis was more common in the men with hypogonadism (45%) than in controls (10%). After 6 months, BMI and bone density measures rose, and total cholesterol, fasting insulin and SHBG fell. There was no untreated comparison group.

src.label: Li et al., Int J Endocrinol

research.text: A 2026 narrative review of peptides used to counter TRT-related suppression of the testes said direct evidence that they restore sperm production or fertility after TRT remains limited. A 2026 review of peptides in sexual medicine noted that gonadorelin was FDA approved but is no longer manufactured.

us.text: Gonadorelin was FDA approved for people as Factrel (1982) and Lutrepulse (1989). FDA lists both as discontinued, and no human gonadorelin product is marketed. The Factrel now on DailyMed is a veterinary product for cattle. Compounded gonadorelin is not FDA approved. As of November 1, 2026.

world.lead: No human gonadorelin product is marketed in the US or Canada; Canada lists Lutrepulse as dormant. EMA’s Article 57 data lists gonadorelin products in 5 EU member states and Northern Ireland, including a nasal product. Veterinary gonadorelin products are listed in both North American countries. It is banned in sport for men at all times.

countries.status: Approved in the past (Factrel 1982, Lutrepulse 1989); both human products discontinued. DailyMed lists only veterinary gonadorelin labels.

after.text: Gonadotrophin-releasing hormone (GnRH, gonadorelin) and its agonist analogues are named under S2.2.1, testosterone-stimulating peptides in males, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. S2 is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) and its substances are non-Specified. The 2027 list keeps this entry, in force January 1, 2027. WADA’s 2027 Monitoring Program adds GnRH analogues in females under 18.

side.text: Published safety data in men are thin. The human Factrel and Lutrepulse labels could not be opened, so their listed side effects are not reported here. In the pump studies, the most reported problem was skin reaction at the pump site.

items.text: skin redness and hardening at the pump site was common with the gonadorelin pump.

items.text: on hCG/hMG, the comparison group tended to have higher testosterone, with more facial acne and breast tenderness, than the pump group.
